description: All matched players count, including those with a blank death country (for example, living players).

c.request: For each player in `appearances` matched to `player`, together with the country they died in (`player.death_country`), total games at first base minus games in center field (`g_1b` − `g_cf`) across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which they exceed that average. Don't round anything. All matched players count, including those with a blank death country (for example, living players).
c.sql:
WITH player_totals AS (
  SELECT p.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total
  FROM appearances AS a
  JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = a.player_id
  WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.player_id, p.death_country
), above_average AS (
  SELECT player_id, total
  FROM player_totals
  WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM player_totals)
)
SELECT SUM(total), AVG(total - (SELECT AVG(total) FROM player_totals))
FROM above_average

b.request: For each player appearing in `appearances` and matched to `player`, regardless of whether `death_country` is blank, sum `g_1b - g_cf` over rows where both values are nonmissing; retain players whose total exceeds the average total across all such players, then return one row containing the sum of their totals and the average of their differences from that overall average, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH player_totals AS (
    SELECT a.player_id, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total
    FROM appearances AS a
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = a.player_id
    WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL
      AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY a.player_id
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total
    FROM player_totals
)
SELECT SUM(pt.total) AS sum_of_totals,
       AVG(pt.total - oa.avg_total) AS average_difference
FROM player_totals AS pt
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS oa
WHERE pt.total > oa.avg_total;

a.request: For every player in `appearances` who matches a `player` record, including those whose death country (`player.death_country`) is blank, total `g_1b` − `g_cf` across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep each player's total together with their death country. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which their totals exceed that average. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH player_totals AS (
    SELECT p.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total
    FROM player p
    JOIN appearances a ON a.player_id = p.player_id
    WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.death_country
), above_average AS (
    SELECT player_id, death_country, total
    FROM player_totals
    WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM player_totals)
)
SELECT SUM(total), AVG(total - (SELECT AVG(total) FROM player_totals))
FROM above_average;

d.request: For every player who can be matched between `appearances` and `player`, including players with a blank `death_country`, sum `g_1b − g_cf` across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep players whose total is above the average total across all matched players. Return one row with two values: the sum of the kept players’ totals and their average excess above that average. Do not round either value.
d.sql:
WITH player_totals AS (
    SELECT p.player_id, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total
    FROM player AS p
    JOIN appearances AS a ON a.player_id = p.player_id
    WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY p.player_id
),
avg_total AS (
    SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total
    FROM player_totals
)
SELECT SUM(pt.total), AVG(pt.total - at.avg_total)
FROM player_totals AS pt
CROSS JOIN avg_total AS at
WHERE pt.total > at.avg_total;
